backlog.title: My backlog
backlog.emptyHint: Add your first game: search the title, pick the platform you own it on, and it shows up here.

backlog.hiddenViewHint: They don't show up in the list or the filters, but they're still yours: ownership doesn't change. “Show again” puts them back.

autoSync.psnWarning: With automatic updates off, the PlayStation connection expires unless you import the library at least once every ten days.

add.title: Add an account
add.description: You can connect more than one account per store: each imports its own library, and your backlog remembers which one a game came from.

unlinkDialog.description: Account {name}. You can keep the games imported from here or delete them: they are two different things.

steam.hint: Paste your Steam profile URL, your SteamID64 or your custom name. The profile must be public, otherwise Steam won't let us read the library.

gog.hint: Open the login page, sign in with your GOG account, then copy the address of the blank page you land on from the browser bar: the code we need is in there. You only do this once.

epic.hint: Open the login page, sign in with your Epic account, then copy the JSON shown on screen — the whole thing is fine, no need to pick the code out of it. You only do this once.

amazon.hint: Open the login page and sign in with your Amazon account — the store is the US one, but a non-US account signs in just fine. Once you land on the amazon.com home page, copy the address from the browser bar. Connecting registers an “AGSLauncher for Windows” device on your Amazon account, which you can remove any time from your Amazon settings.

psn.hint: First sign in to playstation.com in your browser and tick “Trust this browser”, then open the link above: the page answers with a line like '{"npsso":"…"}'. Paste the whole thing, or just the value. An empty npsso or an error means you are not signed in yet. Note: on PlayStation the connection lasts about ten days, then you have to do this again.

unresolved.title: Needs attention ({count})
unresolved.description: These library entries weren't recognised. They're usually beta clients or things that aren't games: you can link them to the right game or hide them, saying what they are.
unresolved.resolveDescription: Search IGDB for the game matching “{name}”({store}). You can also type the IGDB id or paste the game page URL.
unresolved.hiddenHint: Entries you took out of “needs attention”. They stay here after the next imports: if one turns out to be a real game, you can still link it.
